tasks.brief: Allow a workflow execution manifest to omit a Temporal task queue for a non-Temporal runtime. Python and TypeScript must preserve omitted/null behavior and explicit queue values through their manifest APIs. Observability must not index or invent an absent queue. Keep other manifest contracts unchanged.

Reject unknown graph check CI execution IDs locally using the selected revision's tools/development/checks.json as data. Validate the registry shape and fail clearly with declaration/check/unknown ID and registered IDs. Do not execute registry Python. Preserve historical pre-registry snapshot behavior without allowing a working tree or modern snapshot to bypass validation.
tasks.search: CI check execution registry compile_graph snapshot

tasks.brief: Retain bounded safe job observations when trusted CI acceptance rejects required jobs, without relaxing any gate or discarding original failures. Write unique non-overwriting JSON under job-observations/ with kind trusted-ci-job-observation; observedAt, repository, runId, attempt, headRevision, testedRevision, expected, missing, notPassed, observed, totalJobs, omittedJobs, truncatedFields and a limits explanation. Observed jobs retain only id/name/status/conclusion/run_id/run_attempt/head_sha. Prioritize required jobs; at most 100 jobs, strings at most 128 characters, fixed invalid-type/out-of-range markers for malformed fields and integers outside 0 <= x < 10**20. Summary must retain required missing/not-passed identities while staying at most 16,000 characters. Never copy logs, command/URL/freeform payloads or add authority. Workflow artifact naming must preserve run/attempt/evaluator identity and diagnostics with always() across failures. In the workflow, only add one separate diagnostic upload step after the existing acceptance evaluation using the existing upload-action pin; preserve every existing job, step, trigger, permission and setting.

Finish cleanup of an owned process group through repeated SIGINT. Stop/reap owned descendants including signal-resistant children and retain interrupted status/evidence. Do not touch unrelated listeners or processes and do not turn an interruption into success. Preserve normal error behavior.

Record safe bounded native pytest skip diagnostics: phase, classified fixed prerequisite reason codes, and whether details were omitted. Do not store arbitrary reason/exception text, paths, fixture values or personal data. Unclassified skips must remain explicit. Preserve failed status over later teardown skips and retain diagnostics on interruptions; do not weaken required test execution. Public output contract: skipDiagnostics contains at most 3 entries with phase (setup/call/teardown/unknown), reasonCode and detailsOmitted; extra entries increment skipDiagnosticsOmitted. Exact reviewed prerequisite reasons map to node-resolver-prerequisite, isolated-temporal-lane-required, git-prerequisite or temporal-sdk-prerequisite; expected failure maps to expected-failure, otherwise unclassified. Never classify a substring/prefix as an exact reason. Unclassified/expected-failure omit details. A known Node reason is "needs node + the built TS dist (cd packages/typescript && pnpm -r build)"; isolated lane reason is "isolated Temporal lane required". This task covers diagnostic behavior, not unrelated Temporal fixture migration.

An unavailable execution-list read is already bounded by the backend but the console automatically repeats it. Make a selected workflow/environment execution-list read settle after one request and retain the visible error. Keep existing retry behavior for ordinary unrelated reads and preserve routing/query keys.

Write docs/dependent-pull-requests.md and link it from development.md. Explain how to develop, validate, refresh evidence/review and merge a dependent PR under this repository's actual main-target acceptance and squash-merge rules. Include safe read-only inspection commands and distinguish head/base/run/attempt, CI vs review, and PR evidence vs exact-main release evidence. Do not weaken checks, authorize publication or claim a base edit or rerun automatically tests a new base.
tasks.search: dependent prerequisite pull_request main acceptance merge parents

tasks.brief: Extend your earlier CI-registry validation: reject whitespace-only execution IDs and whitespace-only name/verifier fields as malformed registry data. Preserve valid strings, unknown-ID diagnostics, historical snapshot compatibility and every earlier acceptance obligation.

Document your earlier native pytest skip diagnostics in docs/development.md: fields, actual safe codes and classification boundaries, failed-status precedence, bounded omissions, interruption handling, and the fact that classified/skipped evidence cannot satisfy mandatory execution or diagnose a historical cause. Match the behavior of your own earlier patch; do not claim deployment or past CI causes were established.

protocol.extraInvocations: At most 12 documentation grades, 6 grader calibration controls, 6 graph robustness probes; all share one estimate ledger.
protocol.costBasis: Claude CLI reported estimates including all auxiliary models; not a provider invoice. Normal development/code reviews and unmetered Codex orchestration are separate.
protocol.acceptance: Matching reported primary model, applicable in-scope patch, every exact held-out case/build passing and owned cleanup. Docs additionally require 5/5 fixed rubric criteria and no veto.
protocol.successors: Each arm/repeat uses its own applicable predecessor patch, even if earlier held-outs failed. Inapplicable/error predecessors block the successor without another call.
protocol.stopping: No automatic paid retry/correction. Unknown outcome, changed source/model/environment or failed grader calibration stops new work. Budget stop retains unmatched/unreached observations as missing, never passed.
metrics: requested/observed model usage and estimates per accepted patch
declaration changes and automated graph preparation effort
limitations: 12 slots, 10 historical + 2 successors; smaller than proposed 30–50 independent tasks under $50
Python/TypeScript engine pair and shared development-tool tasks are correlated
component filenames are retrospectively localized; solution code and held-outs are withheld from primary context
current frozen third-party dependencies, historical SDK source rebuilt per candidate
same-model rubric is not human review or independent weights
source-window/character/output bounds and fixed search recipe are not adaptive agent exploration
human labor/maintenance time and Codex orchestration charges are not measured
graph maintenance is declaration-change/automated-preparation evidence, not a claim about human effort
no CI reduction, autonomy expansion or runtime/manifest changes

analysis.uncertainty: Retrospective localized component scopes, only two repeats and correlated task families. Sensitivity ranges are not confidence intervals or population effects.
analysis.ciDecision: Keep every mandatory CI/review/release obligation; no autonomy expansion.
analysis.decisionRule: Assembly is only a positive pilot signal if it wins at least two complete task families in both repeats, the declared deterministic policy guards pass, and it costs at most 1.25x search per accepted patch. These are bounded checks, not arbitrary-adversary proof. Even then it remains experimental; no broader adoption or CI change is authorized.
analysis.featureDecision: Retain the existing advisory graph and full verification controls. Keep source assembly experimental: the predeclared adoption signal was not demonstrated; no default or autonomy expansion.
